source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Eat a light meal two hours before collection because fasting does not affect the requested laboratory profile.","B":"Follow the laboratory requirement and complete at least eight hours of fasting before the specimen is collected.","C":"Fast for only one hour because longer fasting can invalidate the lipid measurements in this laboratory profile.","D":"Automatically stop every prescribed morning medicine because all fasting lipid panels require withholding all medications."}}
source_row.rationale: The cited Mayo Clinic Laboratories lipid-panel profile specifies fasting for 8 hours or more. Option B directly follows the laboratory's preparation requirement. Option A ignores the ordered fasting condition, Option C shortens it below the specified interval, and Option D incorrectly turns fasting into a universal instruction to stop prescribed medications; medication directions must follow individualized orders or laboratory instructions.
source_row.source_detail: Mayo Clinic Laboratories Test 616696, Lipid Panel, Serum — Patient Preparation/Profile: fasting is specified as 8 hours or more for the cited fasting lipid profile. Medication instructions are not universally replaced by the fasting requirement and should follow the ordering/laboratory instructions. source_row.stem: A client is scheduled for a serum lipid panel whose laboratory profile specifies “Fasting (8 HR or more).” Which instruction is most accurate?
